title: Nuevo Laredo Puts Millions Into High School Education, Scholarships, and a New Campus
excerpt: Nuevo Laredo is investing millions of pesos in high school education: work at COBAT El Bayito, a new Margarita Maza campus, and scholarships.
content:
Nuevo Laredo is investing millions of pesos in high school education, with new construction, classroom and infrastructure work, and scholarships delivered to students for the 2026-2027 school year, city and state officials announced during a working tour on November 13.

Mayor Carmen Lilia Canturosas Villarreal, joined by Tamaulipas Secretary of Education Miguel Ángel Valdez García, led the tour, which included the groundbreaking for a new high school campus, the opening of a converted campus, and improvements at an existing school.

A new high school for Valle del Paraíso

The centerpiece is the Bachillerato Nacional Margarita Maza, a new high school campus in the Valles del Paraíso neighborhood, an area with high demand for school space. The city donated the land for the campus, which is expected to serve about 500 students at first.

The authorized investment in construction and equipment for the Nuevo Laredo campus is 20,997,600 pesos. It is part of a statewide program building six Margarita Maza campuses — in Altamira, Matamoros, Nuevo Laredo, Reynosa, Tampico, and Victoria — with a total investment of 122,752,286 pesos and a projected reach of more than 2,000 students. The campuses are part of the Plan Integral del Sistema Nacional de Bachillerato de la Nueva Escuela Mexicana (NEM).

More than 4.2 million pesos for COBAT El Bayito

Officials also inaugurated construction and equipment work at the Colegio de Bachilleres de Tamaulipas (COBAT) Plantel 23 “El Bayito,” with a joint investment of more than 4.2 million pesos. The municipal government contributed 2,845,538 pesos for a perimeter wall, a roof structure, a classroom, and restrooms, along with technological equipment.

The tour also included the opening of the Centro de Estudios de Bachillerato building, created by converting the former Secundaria México 2000 campus.

Scholarships for the school year

During the same tour, officials delivered Becas Transformación “Avanza” scholarships for the 2026-2027 school year, a state program that supports Tamaulipas students so they can stay in school.

For families on both sides of the border, the investment matters: Nuevo Laredo is Laredo’s sister city, and many Webb County families have relatives, students, and daily ties across the river. More classroom space and more scholarships on the Mexican side mean more options for young people in a shared border community.

Free opportunity for young people this weekend

The city is also inviting young people ages 15 to 20 to a free grilling course, the Curso Parrillero, on Sunday, November 15, from 8:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m. at Boulevard Díaz Ordaz 2401, Colonia Hipódromo. The course, organized by the Instituto Municipal para el Desarrollo de la Juventud (IMJUVE) with Carnes Don Güero, teaches meat-cut preparation and grill techniques. Registration is through the city’s published form.
